title: Lubricant R&D formula definition
description: Design-space formula object (break-point B3). A formula separates what is CHARGED (inputs) from what the batch actually CONTAINS (products), because a soap thickener is created in situ: fatty acid plus LiOH react during saponification and the soap percentage is a PRODUCT of the batch, not a charge. A 100 % mixture-closure constraint therefore closes the CHARGE, and on grease that constraint does not hold for what determines the product - the charged fatty acid and base are not the same substances as the soap and water that leave the kettle. inputs and products are both non-empty, mixture_basis declares which side the closure applies to, and baseline_process_reference is required so a fraction without a process has no meaning.

inputs.description: Materials charged into the batch. fraction is the charge fraction on a 0..1 basis; a charge-fraction sum near 1 is not evidence that the product composition closes.

products.description: Substances the batch is intended to contain, including in-situ reaction products such as lithium soap. target_fraction is on the same 0..1 basis and reaction_reference names the reaction that produces it.

mixture_basis.description: Which side the 0..1 fraction basis closes: INPUTS means the constraint closes the charge, PRODUCTS means it closes the intended product composition.

baseline_process_reference.description: Required process baseline (kettle, saponification, milling, homogenization settings). A fraction list without a process reference cannot be reproduced or compared.

input_entry.description: One charged material and the role it plays in the batch (for example base_oil, fatty_acid, alkali, additive).

product_entry.description: One intended product substance. A product created in situ binds to the reaction that creates it, so a soap percentage can never be read back as a charge.
